                       425 Grand Concourse RFP Addendum 1
                            RFP issue date: June 29, 2015
                       Addendum 1 issue date: August 13, 2015

Contents of the Addendum

A. Questions and Answers – Enclosed is a summary of questions and answers discussed
at the pre-submission conference that took place on July 31, 2015. Also included are
questions and answers that were sent to the 425 Grand Concourse email address.


B. Phase 1 Executive Summary – The Executive Summary of a Phase I Environmental
Site Assessment completed June 11, 2015.


C. Contact Information – Contact Information is provided for those individuals who
attended the pre-submission conference and indicated that they are willing to share their
contact information.


D. Architectural Elements – Brief description and photos of architectural elements from
the former Public School 31, which are currently stored at the New York Botanical
Garden and must be incorporated into the design for the 425 Grand Concourse
development project.




                                            1
A. Questions and Answers – Enclosed is a summary of questions and answers discussed
at the pre-submission conference that took place July 31, 2015. Also included are
questions and answers that were sent to the 425 Grand Concourse email address.


Residential and Retail/Community Facility Program

Q1: Are we allowed to propose a mix of rental and homeownership units?
A1: HPD does not have a preference. If the proposal includes homeownership, it would
be helpful if it was clear that that was preferred by local stakeholders.

Q2: Regarding the maximum 15% studio apartments and minimum 15% 3-
bedroom apartments, do these requirements remain if a substantial supportive
housing component is being proposed?
A2: The New Construction term sheets allow a maximum of 15% of studio-sized units.
HPD is open to proposals that include a supportive housing component of up to 30% of
the total units in the project, although it is not a preference for this RFP. If a proposal has
a supportive housing component, HPD is open to seeing more than 15% studio
apartments if necessary to serve the special needs population identified.

Q3: Will HPD be engaging Hostos Community College about the Development Site?
A3: HPD has informed Hostos about the RFP, but it will be up to the developer to decide
whether or not to reach out to Hostos. HPD is looking for active ground floor uses on the
Grand Concourse side and we are open to community facilities on the Walton Avenue
side, so it is up to the applicant to choose the ground-floor uses you want to propose and
to reach out to potential tenants.

Q4. Is there any preference for the types of commercial storefront businesses facing
the Grand Concourse?
A4. HPD does not have a specific preference for the commercial storefront businesses on
the Grand Concourse, but they should serve to activate and encourage activity on the
Grand Concourse.


Zoning/Land Use/Environment/Outreach Process

Q5: Has there been any consideration of inclusionary zoning for the Site?
A5: HPD anticipates that the block will be rezoned to C6-3. A decision regarding
inclusionary has not yet been finalized, so applicants should assume the C6-3 zoning for
proposals. Long-term affordability is a goal, so in considering the extent of affordability,
we will certainly take into account the length of affordability guaranteed in exchange for
any subsidy required.

Q6. What is the maximum zoning floor area for this Site?
A6. The intention is to rezone the block to C6-3. Please refer to the New York City
Zoning Resolution for additional information.

                                               2
Q7: Should we take into account the impact on parking requirements of potential
zoning changes?
A7: For your proposal, please assume the parking requirements that are currently in effect
under the New York City Zoning Resolution.

Q8: During the ULURP process, are HPD and the developer co-applicants?
A8: HPD will be the applicant for ULURP, but may request certain documentation such
as plans and drawings from the developer during the process. This project will follow the
same process as most HPD RFPs.

Q9: Does the developer need to engage the Community Board in discussions related
to this project?
A9: Prior to selection of a Development Team, no engagement with the Community
Board is necessary. After a developer is chosen for the project, the team will need to
engage the Community Board and make a presentation of their proposal for the
development site.

Q10: Is there a survey available for the Site? If so, is it topographical? Are there
borings on the Site?
A10: HPD does not provide surveys for its RFP sites. This is the responsibility of the
developer.

Q11. We are aware of cost estimates prepared several years ago for the abatement
and remediation of hazardous building materials including asbestos and lead paint.
Those estimates were well into the millions of dollars. Were those materials
removed from the site and disposed of properly or if they remain on-site and have
been mixed in with other demolition debris? And if they are found to still be present
on-site, is it the respondent’s responsibility to include those removal and disposal
costs in the financial model or will the city be covering those expenses?
A11. HPD retained a contractor to demolish the existing building and asbestos was
removed from the building properly. There are no rules/guidelines when demoing a
building for lead paint. Any additional environmental remediation work is the
responsibility of the selected developer.

Q12: Has a Phase 1 been conducted for the Site?
A12: Yes, a Phase 1 was completed for this site and the Executive Summary is included
in this addendum.

Q13. Aside from removing the existing wall and site infill are there any
environmental factors that need to be considered so that it can be incorporated into
the design and budgeting plan?
A13. A Phase 1 was completed for this site and the Executive Summary is included in
this addendum. The selected development team is responsible for any necessary
environmental work.




                                            3
Design/Building Configuration

Q14: The design portion of the RFP is very subjective. The RFP also mentions
creating something that feels iconic, similar to the PS 31 building that had to be
demolished. Is HPD looking for something that is more contextual, traditional, or
modern with the design?
A14: HPD is not asking the developer to design a collegiate gothic building or recreate
P.S. 31. As indicated in the RFP, “Overall design should be inspiring and create a sense
of place. Respondents are encouraged to create a signature building that is respectful of
its surroundings.” HPD would like to see the applicant’s interpretation of an iconic and
inspiring building.

Q15: Is HPD open to proposals with multiple buildings on the site?
A15: HPD is open to the best design for the site and it is up to the development team to
propose what they think is the best design.

Q16. Will roof top water cooler systems be prohibited from the design specification?
A16. Roof top water cooler systems are permitted.


Garrison Park and Walkway

Q17: Does the RFP require the developer to look at Garrison Playground, other
than the adjacent walkway?
A17: The expectation is that the Parks Department will be responsible for rehabilitating
the playground, but the RFP encourages applicants to consider setting aside a portion of
funds to help with ongoing park maintenance and programming. This is a competitive
factor in the RFP and it is up to the applicant to determine how much will be proposed for
this purpose.

Q18. Per the information session – no rehabilitation is required for Garrison
Playground (only a maintenance and operation plan is required), in order to
provide a symbiotic design of the site it would make sense to provide minimal
rehabilitation to the playground. Will the NYC DPR entertain the option of
providing funding (90%) to rehabilitate the playground so it blends into the new
design?
A18. Applicants are welcome to propose additional funding to contribute to the
rehabilitation of the playground; however, rehabilitation planning and coordination with
the NYC DPR will occur once a development team is selected.

Q19: Is there a contact person at NYC Parks and Recreation that we ask for
information about Garrison Playground?
A19: Questions for the NYC Parks Department should be directed to the 425 Grand
Concourse RFP email address. We can forward the questions to Parks.




                                            4
Q20: Will we be able to know the intentions of the Parks Department for the
rehabilitation of Garrison Playground?
A20: HPD is in regular contact with Parks about plans for Garrison Playground. We do
not expect rehabilitation plans to be finalized by the time submissions are due.
Therefore, proposals should assume that the Playground will remain at its current grade
level and a similar configuration of uses.

Q21. Please provide the design team with any NYC DPR requirements which the
design must incorporate should the design address rehabilitation of the park as well
as for operation and maintenance of the Garrison Playground.
A21. Design requirements will be identified and coordinated with the NYC DPR once a
development team is selected. Contributions for the operation and maintenance of the
Playground are a competitive factor in the RFP and it is up to the applicant to determine
how much will be proposed for this purpose.


Architectural Elements

Q22. Please provide the date and location (digital or in person) when the
information of existing elements (signage; gargoyles etc.) will be provided to
designers for incorporation into the RFP.
A22. Please see the information included in this addendum.

Q23: Will HPD provide information related to costs of transporting the
architectural pieces from the Botanical Gardens to the Development Site?
A23: This cost will be insignificant compared to the overall cost of the development.

Q24: Will the architectural pieces from the former PS 31 building need to be
restored?
A24: There is no requirement for restoration, but this will depend on the developer’s
strategy for incorporating the pieces into the project design.

Q25: Can we go to see the architectural pieces? Will you be able to provide a catalog
of photos of the architectural pieces from PS 31?
A25: The architectural elements are not available for in-person viewing. Please see the
information included in this addendum.

Q26: How specific should we be with the proposal for incorporating the
architectural pieces from the former PS 31 building?
A26: HPD does not expect a high level of detail in the proposal. A paragraph that is
conceptual and indicates the general plan for the architectural elements is sufficient.

Q27: Will SHPO be involved in this project?
A27: We do not expect SHPO will be involved.




                                             5
Financing

Q28: Will HDC waive the cap on the total amount of the second mortgage?
A28: HDC would prefer to see proposals that stay under the cap.

Q29: Is the mortgage tied to the appraised value of the land? Can you subdivide the
residential and the commercial components of the development and is it then
possible for the note to be tied solely to the residential part?
A29: The enforcement mortgage will be sized based on the HPD appraised value of the
land minus the acquisition cost. No, applicants should assume the enforcement mortgage
will be tied to both the residential and commercial components.

Q30: Can development teams apply for 421A?
A30: Development teams may apply for 421A. Please note that applicants may be asked
to revise their submission based on any changes to the exemption after the extension
period expires in January.


Other

Q31: Considering the number of RFP submission deadlines coming up, is there a
possibility of extending the deadline for 425 Grand Concourse?
A31: No, the intention is to keep the same deadline.

Q32: Are there any M/WBE requirements or bonuses for this project?
A32: No. There are not any M/WBE requirements or bonuses for this RFP.

1.0        EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
     Parsons Brinckerhoff (PB) has performed a Phase I environmental site assessment (ESA) in
     conformance with the scope and limitations of 40 CFR Part 312 (Standards and Practices for All
     Appropriate Inquiries) and ASTM Method E 1527-13 (Standard Practice for Environmental Site
     Assessments) of the Former PS 31 School property (the Site) at 425 Grand Concourse, Bronx,
     NY 10451 for NYC Housing Preservation & Development (HPD). No party other than those
     listed in Section 2.8 may rely upon any information or opinion contained in this report. Any
     exceptions to, or deletions from, this practice are described in Section 2.5 of this report. This
     executive summary briefly discusses the conclusions of this assessment. Reading it should not
     be considered a substitute for reading the entire report. Only the report in its entirety should be
     relied upon to provide complete information regarding PB's observations when reviewing the
     environmental conditions for this Site.

     This assessment has revealed no evidence of recognized environmental conditions in
     connection with the Site. The assessment did however; reveal evidence of three Historical
     Recognized Environmental Condition (HREC).

          1. A NYS Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC) spill number was opened
             in Aug. 2007 and was related to leaking pipes associated with a 10,000-gallon, fuel oil
               above ground storage tank (AST). The spill was investigated and cleaned up and the
               spill number closed Jan. 2008. Based on closure, this spill is identified as an on-Site
               HREC.

          2. A NYSDEC spill was reported at the Hostos Community College building at the
             corner of Walton Ave. and E. 144th St., which is adjacent southwest to the Site. The
             spill was related to the presence of two 2,000-gallon, diesel USTs that were
             reportedly associated with a former gas station on this property. A preliminary
             investigation confirmed soil contamination around the tanks. The tanks were
             cleaned out and removed. It was determined the leak was from the associated
             piping. Post excavation samples indicated limited contamination and the impacted
             soils were removed and the excavation back filled with clean sand. The spill number
             was closed March 14, 2006. Based on closure, this spill is identified as an off-Site
             HREC.

          3. A NYSDEC spill was reported at the Hostos Community College Trailer #5, 427
             Walton Ave., which is adjacent west of the Site, across Walton Ave. A 10,000-
             gallon, #6 fuel oil UST was closed in place on March 25, 2008. A spill in the
             basement was observed and a spill number opened April 14, 2008. Soil and


PB Project No. 183749P                           -1-                                    Parsons Brinckerhoff
                                                                                              June 11, 2015
Parsons Brinckerhoff

               groundwater samples collected adjacent to the tank did not indicate impacts.
               Additional soil borings were drilled and soil/groundwater samples collected. No
               significant impacts were found and the spill number was closed on June 24, 2010.
               Based on closure, this spill is identified as an off-Site HREC.

     Data gaps occur when the consultant is unable to identify information required to satisfy
     objectives of this assessment. Data gaps may result from incompleteness in and of the activities
     required by the ESA standard, or by limiting conditions encountered during completion of the
     work. The ESA Standard requires that data gaps be identified in the report when they
     significantly impact the ability of the consultant to identify RECs at the site. There was no Key
     Site Manager available for an interview and no access to the Site was provided. However,
     information obtained from other sources has allowed PB to sufficiently assess the conditions
     associated with the Property and to make an informed decision regarding the identification of
     potential RECs. Therefore, the absence of a Key Site Manager and no access to the Site are not
     identified as significant data gaps.

     The Site is located in an urban area of the Bronx that is characterized by mixed-use residential
     and commercial buildings, a community college, warehouses and a NYC Transit System
     building. The building on the Site is PS 31, which has been used as a public school since at least
     1903. The building is currently being demolished to make way for construction of affordable
     housing.

     Surrounding property use includes mixed-use commercial and residential to the east, across the
     Grand Concourse; a U-Haul facility and associated parking lot adjacent south, across E. 144th
     St.; a loft/warehouse and a Hostos Community College temporary classroom adjacent west,
     across Walton Ave.; and the Garrison Playground adjacent north.

     Based on a review of available Sanborn fire insurance maps, aerial photographs, topographic
     maps and city directories, the Site was developed with multiple dwellings prior to the current
     building, which is visible by 1903. Surrounding property uses have included some manufacturing
     processes in addition to both residential and commercial uses. No information was found that
     would indicate environmental impacts from these surrounding property uses.

     According to regulatory records, the building was heated with #4 fuel oil stored in a 10,000-
     gallon AST that was located in the basement. Regulatory records indicate that the tank was
     installed in 1957. No information was provided regarding previous sources of heat.

     The Site is identified on the NY Spills database for a reported spill that occurred in 2007. During
     investigation of the spill, the 10,000-gallon AST was drained and cleaned out. Post excavation
     soil samples did not indicate a significant concern and the spill number was closed in 2008.
     Based on closure, this spill is identified as a HREC. The Site is also listed on the NYSDEC PBS

PB Project No. 183749P                           -2-                                    Parsons Brinckerhoff
                                                                                              June 11, 2015
Parsons Brinckerhoff

     database for the 10,000-gallon tank. No regulatory records were identified within the target
     search area that would indicate a potential impact to the Site.

     Based on this assessment, no additional action or assessment is recommended.

                                                                                             2
D. Architectural Elements – Brief description and photos of architectural elements from the
former Public School 31, which are currently stored at the New York Botanical Garden and must
be incorporated into the design for the 425 Grand Concourse development project.

19 items were delivered to the New York Botanical Garden. The summary and descriptions
below are very rough approximations. Please refer to the photos included below for a sense of
size/bulk.

   1) Public School 31 sign (in three pieces): together approximately 10 ft. by 2 ft. and
      weighing approximately 900 lbs.

   2) Standing gargoyle: approximately 3 ft. tall and 9 inches to 1 ft. in diameter (no base)

   3) Multiple heads with full base: approximately 2 ft. by 3 ft.-between approximately 100-
      150 lbs., possibly more.

   4) Multiple heads with partial or no base: approximately 1 ft. by 2 ft. and perhaps 75-100
      lbs.

   5) “Boys” sign: approximately 2 ½ by 2 ft. approximately 150 lbs., possibly more

   6) Wood pieces including sign: approximately 6 inches by 8 ft.
